guidance: A field reader, not a validator: the bytes are trusted and a frame that parses is not necessarily well formed for its purpose. A frame check sequence is reported only when the last four octets reproduce the CRC-32 of the rest, which most captures have already stripped. VLAN identifiers are printed as the field carries them, including 4095, which IEEE 802.1Q reserves. The inner protocol line summarises the first bytes only. This page reads no traffic and makes no capture.
method: The frame is read at the octet offsets IEEE 802.3 gives it. Octets 0 to 5 are the destination address, 6 to 11 the source, and 12 and 13 are the type or length field: 1536 and above is an EtherType, 1500 and below is a payload length, and 1501 to 1535 is undefined, which the page reports instead of guessing. The group bit is the low bit of the first octet and the local bit the next one, so a destination with the group bit is multicast, all ones is broadcast, and a source with the group bit set is called out because a transmitted frame never carries one. A four-octet tag follows the addresses when the field is 0x8100 (802.1Q) or 0x88a8 (802.1ad): the two-octet tag protocol identifier, then a tag control information word of three priority bits, one drop-eligible bit and twelve VLAN identifier bits, and tags stack until the field stops being a tag identifier, up to eight. An IEEE 802.3 length field is followed by a three-octet LLC header whose control field is one octet in the U format, when its low two bits are 11, and two otherwise; when both service access points are 0xaa and the control byte is 0x03, a SNAP header supplies a three-octet organisation code and a two-octet protocol identifier that is read as an EtherType. With a length field the payload is exactly the declared number of octets and everything after it is padding, so the split is shown; an Ethernet II header carries no length, so any padding to the 60-octet minimum is inside the payload count and the page says so. The frame check sequence is the 32-bit CRC of every octet before it, polynomial 0x04c11db7 reflected as 0xedb88320, initial value all ones and complemented at the end, stored least significant octet first; the page reports one only when the last four octets reproduce that value, because capture tools normally strip it, and a frame under 60 octets without the FCS is marked a runt. The inner protocol line names IPv4, IPv6 or ARP from the first bytes only: version, protocol or next header, and addresses. Ports, transport headers and payloads are not read, the preamble and the inter-frame gap are not part of the frame, and nothing is captured, stored or sent.
